title: Choose a clear call to action
Check your website link
action: Open the website link on each business listing and correct any outdated address.

title: Update holiday hours
action: Check your next holiday opening hours and update your business listing.

title: Add a real business photo
action: Choose a recent, accurate photo of your business and add it to your listing.

title: Review your service area
action: Compare your public service area with where you actually work and fix mismatches.

title: Check your main category
action: Choose the business category that most accurately describes your core service.

title: Add your core services
action: List the services customers can actually book, using their everyday names.

title: Check your directory details
action: Compare your name, address, and phone on your three most important listings.

title: Read your latest reviews
action: Read your last ten reviews and note the questions and praise that repeat.

title: Answer a customer review
action: Reply to one review with a helpful, personal response that respects privacy.

title: Find one local partner
action: List a complementary local business that serves customers you can help.

title: Make your phone number tappable
action: Test the phone number on your site from a mobile phone. Make sure it opens a call.

title: Check your contact details
action: Compare your contact page with your current phone, email, hours, and address.

title: Remove a broken link
action: Click your main navigation links and repair the first broken destination you find.

title: Shorten your inquiry form
action: Remove one field you do not need for the first conversation.

title: Explain what happens after a form
action: Add a realistic response time next to your inquiry form.

title: Write a useful page title
action: Give one service page a title that names its service and business.

title: Describe an important image
action: Add helpful alternative text to one meaningful image. Leave decorative images silent.

title: Check your page on a phone
action: Read a service page on your phone and fix text that is too small or clipped.

title: Make your button easy to tap
action: Check that your main mobile button has enough space around it and is easy to use.

title: Back up your site
action: Confirm you have a current backup and know how to restore it.

title: Describe your best-fit customer
action: Write one sentence naming the people your business helps most.

title: Name the problem you solve
action: Write the customer problem in words you hear in real conversations.

title: Write one clear service description
action: Explain one service without jargon, including what the customer receives.

title: Replace a vague claim
action: Replace “best quality” with an accurate detail about your process or product.

title: Answer the price question
action: Explain how pricing works and what a customer needs to get an estimate.

title: Answer one common objection
action: Add an honest answer to a question that frequently delays a purchase.

title: Explain your service area
action: Tell customers where you work and any limits they should know about.

title: Write a three-step plan
action: Describe how someone starts, what you do, and what they receive.

title: Make a guarantee specific
action: If you offer a guarantee, state its time frame, coverage, and conditions clearly.

title: Read your copy aloud
action: Read a page aloud and simplify sentences that sound unnatural.

title: Request testimonial permission
action: Ask one customer if you may publish their genuine feedback with attribution.

title: Show a completed project
action: Choose a real project and explain what you did without overstating results.

title: Explain your role
action: On one portfolio example, name the parts your team actually handled.

title: Add a real team introduction
action: Write a short introduction for someone customers will actually work with.

title: Check a public claim
action: Find one number or claim on your site and confirm that you can support it.

title: Show your process
action: Share a simple picture or explanation of how you perform a service.

title: Update an old portfolio item
action: Check that a project link and description are still accurate.

title: Add a useful customer question
action: Publish an answer to a real question from a recent customer.

title: Clarify a service limitation
action: Tell customers about one boundary that helps them decide if you are a fit.

title: Ask why someone chose you
action: Ask a willing customer what helped them decide and record their exact answer privately.

title: List ten customer questions
action: Write down ten questions customers ask before they buy.

title: Answer one question in a post
action: Pick one question and write a short, useful answer with a practical next step.

title: Create a before-and-after explanation
action: Describe a real change you made, with permission and accurate context.

title: Write a seasonal reminder
action: Share one useful tip related to the next season your customers prepare for.

title: Repurpose a useful answer
action: Turn an existing answer into a short post for one channel your customers use.

title: Add a clear next step to a post
action: Link one helpful article to the related service or contact action.

title: Update an old article
action: Check dates, links, and facts in one older post and correct outdated information.

title: Make a content list you can keep
action: Choose four useful topics you can realistically publish over the next month.

title: Use your customer’s language
action: Replace one technical term with the wording a customer used in a question.

title: Share a useful checklist
action: Write three steps a customer can follow to prepare for your service.

title: Choose an email signup benefit
action: Write down exactly what someone gets by joining your email list.

title: Write a clear signup invitation
action: Explain the content and frequency people can expect before they subscribe.

title: Review your consent wording
action: Check that signup language describes the messages you intend to send.

title: Write your welcome email
action: Thank the subscriber, deliver the promised resource, and explain what comes next.

title: Test your signup form
action: Subscribe with your own test address and verify the confirmation and delivery.

title: Check the unsubscribe path
action: Use a test subscription to confirm someone can easily stop receiving emails.

title: Write one useful email
action: Answer one customer question and include a single relevant next step.

title: Segment by stated interest
action: Use interests subscribers willingly provided to make one message more relevant.

title: Remove an outdated promise
action: Check your signup offer and remove anything you no longer deliver.

title: Check your reply address
action: Reply to your own test newsletter and confirm it reaches a monitored inbox.

title: Write a 30-second introduction
action: Name who you help, their problem, and the next step in a short script.

title: Record a simple introduction
action: Use your phone to record the script somewhere quiet with good light.

title: Caption your video
action: Add accurate captions and check names, prices, and service terms.

title: Add a video transcript
action: Publish a readable text version next to a useful business video.

title: Answer one question on camera
action: Record a brief answer to a real customer question.

title: Check your video on mobile
action: Play your video on a phone and verify that controls and captions work.

title: Plan a short podcast episode
action: Pick one customer problem and outline an answer with a practical action.

title: Ask a guest for permission
action: Confirm a guest is comfortable with recording and your intended publication.

title: Make a useful episode title
action: Name the problem or outcome discussed instead of using only an episode number.

title: Add links to an episode
action: Include the resources actually mentioned in the recording.

title: Count your recent inquiries
action: Count inquiries over a representative period and note the source of the count.

title: Define a qualified inquiry
action: Write a simple definition of the kind of inquiry your business can serve.

title: Track booked appointments
action: Record appointments using a consistent definition and time period.

title: Ask how customers found you
action: Add a simple source question to your normal customer conversation.

title: Review one stalled inquiry
action: Look at a recent inquiry that did not progress and identify one possible obstacle.

title: Compare like-for-like periods
action: Compare results across similar time periods, noting seasonality and changes.

title: Check campaign link labels
action: Use consistent campaign labels so incoming traffic can be understood.

title: Record a marketing change
action: Write down what changed and when so later comparisons have context.

title: Review one conversion path
action: Follow one path from a visitor’s first page to a completed inquiry.

title: Set a monthly review date
action: Choose a date to review inquiries, bookings, and the work completed.

title: List your marketing tasks
action: Write the tasks you keep postponing, without trying to solve all of them.

title: Choose one task to finish
action: Pick a small task connected to your current business goal.

title: Estimate your available time
action: Set a realistic amount of time you can spend on marketing this week.

title: Name your most useful offer
action: Choose an offer that serves customers well and fits your business capacity.

title: Check your booking capacity
action: Decide how much new work your team can handle before increasing promotion.

title: Plan a simple customer interview
action: Write five open questions about the customer’s needs and decision process.

title: Set a clear project scope
action: Write the deliverable, who approves it, and what counts as finished.

title: Review recurring services
action: Check what each recurring marketing service provides and whether you still need it.

title: Document a repeatable task
action: Write the steps for one task you or your team perform every month.

title: Choose next month’s focus
action: Review what worked and choose the next priority tied to your business goal.
